chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"Al-maḍmaḍah and al-istinshāq are neither an obligation nor a sunnah (prophetic tradition); rather, what is upon you is to wash what is outwardly visible."

Thus, the meaning of his saying, "nor a sunnah (prophetic tradition)," is that it is not from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) whose omission is impermissible. As for its being a bidʿah to perform it, the report does not indicate that.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقُ: drawing water into the nose during wudu (ablution)
key_terms.سُنَّةً: a sunnah (prophetic tradition); here, a non-obligatory or non-binding prescribed practice
key_terms.فَرِيضَةً: an obligatory act required by law

ai.seo_question: Are al-maḍmaḍah and al-istinshāq obligatory in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are not obligatory parts of wudu (ablution), nor are they from the binding sunnah (prophetic tradition) that may not be left. The clarification explains that the report negates obligation, not permissibility, so doing them is not shown here to be a bidʿah.
